Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — onboarding, SLA & buyer authorization

Hi Janet —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, attached is a starting private-offer package you can share with procurement and legal. High-level options we recommend for CloudWave:

- Option A (24 months, recommended): 24-month term, consumption-based billing with a 12% unit discount vs public rates, includes $25k onboarding credit for migration/workshops.
- Option B (36 months): 36-month committed spend with 18% upfront discount (applied as monthly billing credit) + extended onboarding credits and a 60-day rollout SLA for ramp assistance.

SLA: we can commit to a 99.9% availability target with a financial credit framework (credit applied as monthly invoice reduction). Ben and I have a suggested SLA clause in the attached draft_po_terms.pdf.

Co-sell: John Holden (AWS AM) is on-copy in case you want co-sell uplift and marketplace listing support — co-sell can accelerate procurement and provide buyer introductions.

Procurement/practicalities we need from you: buyer authorization matrix (who signs for PO vs who signs for SOW), procurement contact (I saw procurement@cloudwave.com), and legal review timeline. If CloudWave prefers a 24-month term we'll thread that into the private offer request and provide a DocuSign-ready PO to speed signature.

Attachments: pricing_matrix.xlsx, onboarding_playbook.pdf, draft_po_terms.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm the preferred term (24 vs 36 months) and share the names/titles required for buyer approval? Once we have that, we'll prepare the private-offer package and route to AWS for acceptance.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — onboarding, SLA & buyer authorization

Hi Aditya,

Appreciate the clear options. A couple of clarifying asks from procurement/legal: 

1) Term: CloudWave would prefer a 24-month (two-year) term rather than 12 — is the 12% discount your floor for 24 months? We want to understand delta vs 36 months.
2) SLA: we require 99.95% for production workloads; if Redwood can do 99.9%, procurement will ask for remediation language and credits. Can you propose specific credit tiers (e.g., 10% invoice credit for <99.9, 30% for <99.5)?
3) Data residency: can you confirm processing and logging of inference requests will remain in AWS us-east-1 unless otherwise requested?
4) Purchase flow: procurement needs a PO-ready private-offer document + a statement of work for onboarding milestones. Legal will redline the SOW.

I've attached our internal procurement intake form to speed approvals. Copying our procurement mailbox. Janet Morales
Director of IT Procurement
Janet.Morales@cloudwave.com
procurement@cloudwave.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: AWS Marketplace private offer — onboarding, SLA & buyer authorization

Aditya / Marissa —

Thanks — quick internal thoughts:

- Term/price: 24 months with 12% off is acceptable. If CloudWave pushes for parity with 36-month economics, we can offer a 2% incremental discount (i.e., 14%) if they commit to a minimum monthly run-rate after month 3. Avoid deep concessions on upfront credits unless we get a committed usage baseline.
- SLA: weight toward 99.9% (industry-standard for our hosted tiers). For 99.95 we can entertain with a 30% credit tier at <99.5 but that increases our operational risk. Suggest: publish 99.9% in PO and agree a short-term evaluation (60 days post-onboard) to revisit. Insert a simple credit table: <99.9 = 10% credit, <99.5 = 25% credit, <99.0 = 50% credit.
- Data residency: confirm us-east-1 by default. If CloudWave requires multi-region or EU residency we should route them to our Private offering (higher TCO).
- Co-sell: loop in John Holden (AWS) for co-sell package. If AWS supports a marketplace private offer co-sell uplift we can add that to our joint GTM plan; securing that will help get buyer exec sponsorship.

I've sketched a short draft of PO language (see draft_po_terms.pdf). Recommend we propose the 24-month option with the 12% off and the onboarding credit; highlight a 60-day SLA evaluation clause.

Ben
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi team —

Happy to help. A few notes from the AWS Marketplace side:

- Private offer flow: seller submits private offer, buyer signs, AWS accepts the private offer on the marketplace. The acceptance step can be a blocker if terms deviate from standard marketplace billing — so keep SOW and billing flow aligned with marketplace expectations.
- Co-sell: we can provide co-sell enablement and partner credits for qualified deals. Please include our Partner ID in the PO/package and confirm seller is enrolled in the AWS ISV Accelerate program (if not, we can do a fast-track).
- SLA language: marketplace itself doesn't enforce runtime SLA; that's between buyer and seller. AWS will prefer simpler credit tables and clear acceptance criteria.

Attached: AWS_co_sell_checklist.pdf — it lists the artifacts we need on our side (customer exec sponsor, one-pager, technical contact, expected ARR).

If helpful, I can set a brief call with the CloudWave procurement team to walk them through the private-offer acceptance steps.

Best,
John Holden
Senior Partner Manager, AWS
john.holden@amazon.com
